# LLM Pricing

> Pricing, quality leaderboards and selection tools for 1359+ LLM/chat models across 230 providers. Data from models.dev and Artificial Analysis.

## Overview

- Models: 1359
- Providers: 230
- Provider quotes: 8909
- Data synced: 2026-10-23

## About

LLM Pricing aggregates and normalizes API pricing, capabilities and quality benchmarks for large language / chat models, so you can compare price, capability and every provider's quote in one place.

Methodology:
- Models are merged into canonical entries by normalized name (a model hosted on many providers is one entry with per-provider quotes).
- Blended unit price = input x 0.75 + output x 0.25 (approximate typical usage mix).
- Official price = the quote from the lab's own API. When the lab does not sell a model directly (open-weights releases, superseded snapshots), no official price is shown and third-party quotes appear only as channels.
- Providers are tiered: first-party (the lab itself), cloud platforms, and third-party gateways. The lowest price is taken from paid channels; $0 channels are listed separately (free tiers usually have rate limits).
- Capability flags are tri-state: supported / unsupported / unknown — never conflated.

## Data sources

- Pricing & capabilities: models.dev (MIT licensed).
- Official media generation pricing: vendor pricing pages (81 models, checked 2026-09-29).
- Quality, coding, agentic, speed & cost-per-task scores: Artificial Analysis.
- Real-world usage (30-day tokens): OpenRouter.
- Data is refreshed regularly (last sync 2026-10-23); prices are indicative — always confirm on each provider's official page.

## Key pages

- [Pricing](https://llmpricing.dev/en/): compare price, capability and every provider's quote for all models
- [Leaderboards](https://llmpricing.dev/en/leaderboards/): intelligence, coding, value, cost per task, speed, usage
- [Value frontier](https://llmpricing.dev/en/frontier/): best intelligence per dollar
- [Providers](https://llmpricing.dev/en/providers/): first-party, cloud and gateway providers
- [Compare](https://llmpricing.dev/en/compare/): compare two or more models with radar profiles and metric tables
- [Releases](https://llmpricing.dev/en/releases/): a dated feed of recent model releases, each linking to the model's page

## Tools

- [Cost calculator](https://llmpricing.dev/en/tools/cost/): estimate monthly API cost across providers from token usage and cache hit rate
- [Token counter](https://llmpricing.dev/en/tools/token/): exact token counts for OpenAI tokenizers (o200k/cl100k) plus labeled estimates for other models, and per-model cost
- [Subscription vs API](https://llmpricing.dev/en/tools/subscription/): whether an AI subscription beats pay-as-you-go for your usage (ranges, not single points)
- [AI subscription prices](https://llmpricing.dev/en/subscriptions/): consumer plans and quotas for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Copilot and more

## Articles

- [Always-on AI agents explained: Claude Duet, Grok Bot, Muse, dots and Gemini Spark](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/always-on-ai-agents-explained/): Agents that run on their own cloud computer, keep working after you close the app and ask before they act. What the five main products do, where they differ and what each costs to start.
- [Claude Duet vs Grok Bot: what each costs and how the limits work](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/claude-duet-vs-grok-bot/): Which plans include each agent, who can use it today, how the usage limits work, and what the plan fee buys at API list prices.
- [What is Claude Duet? What Anthropic's proactive agent does](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-claude-duet/): A separate Claude app that sends a morning brief, watches your connected accounts, runs tasks on its own cloud computer and asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes.
- [What is ChatGPT dots? OpenAI's always-on agents explained](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-chatgpt-dots/): A named agent inside ChatGPT that holds ongoing goals, researches in the background, runs scheduled checks, works in 4,000+ apps and follows rules you set for when to act and when to ask.
- [What is Meta Muse? Meta's personal AI agent explained](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-meta-muse/): An agent you message like a person. It plans toward goals, opens a browser, fills forms, negotiates and pays with a one-time card, and a separate Sentinel agent approves what leaves its VM.
- [What are GLM 5.3 Uncensored and GLM 5.3 Flash Uncensored?](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-glm-5-3-uncensored/): Two weight-edited GLM-5.3 derivatives that refuse far less than the base models. What abliteration changes, which base each starts from, what each costs, and the limits that still apply.
- [What is Grok Bot? xAI's AI teammates explained](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-grok-bot/): Named Bots with a browser, files and a terminal in the cloud, several working in parallel, learning workflows from a single demonstration and checking back when they need approval.
- [What is Gemini Spark? Google's 24/7 agent, now Task in Gemini](https://llmpricing.dev/en/articles/what-is-gemini-spark/): Recurring tasks, triggers and skills that run in Google's cloud while your devices are off, with a local or remote browser and confirmation before sending, buying or editing shared files.

## Data & API

Normalized data is published as free static JSON (CC BY 4.0, no key required):
- [Models JSON](https://llmpricing.dev/api/models.json): every model with prices, blended unit price, context, capabilities, quality scores and usage
- [Providers JSON](https://llmpricing.dev/api/providers.json): every provider with tier, model count, SDK and API base
- [API & MCP docs](https://llmpricing.dev/en/api/): field reference, code examples and how to consume the data from an MCP-enabled agent
